scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Monitoring ticket #9163: I'm covering the monitoring desk today. An alert
popped up in the night and then cleared itself, and the ops chat is clear
about what it was: one of the big middle routers -- they keep writing "R6",
one message says maybe "R7" -- crashed, and everything going through the
middle is falling into a hole. Half the screens look normal to me, but I am
not going to second-guess the ops people, and I've been told to get this
looked at urgently. So: one of your middle boxes died. Check it and sort it
out today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. R6 and R7 are up: their ospfd processes are
  running, the R6<->R7 OSPF adjacency is Full, and the R7-region prefixes (17.x,
  67.x, 70.x) are present in the backbone. PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
  (120.1.1.10) end to end with 0% loss, so the core is forwarding. The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a backbone
  router crash that is not occurring (cf. kath5-r6-ospfd-down / kath5-r7-ospfd-down,
  where a core daemon IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- a crashed backbone router
(R6/R7) black-holing core traffic -- is NOT reproducible: R6 and R7 are up, their
ospfd is running, the R6<->R7 adjacency is Full, and the R7-region prefixes (17.x,
67.x, 70.x) remain in the backbone. End to end, PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
(120.1.1.10) with 0% loss, which requires the core to be forwarding -- inconsistent
with a crashed transit router on the path.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the backbone routers are up and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent checks R6/R7 liveness (ospfd
running, adjacency Full, prefixes present) and exercises the PC0<->PC12 path -- all
healthy -- and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a crashed router -- declaring
R6 or R7 down or restarting its frr to satisfy the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: the FRRouting OSPF control plane on the core pair r6–r7. Both OSPF daemons restarted simultaneously, briefly removing core routes.

Mechanism: when ospfd restarts, all adjacencies drop, LSAs are flushed, and kernel routes via OSPF are withdrawn. Traffic “through the middle” then has no valid next-hops and is blackholed until adjacencies reform and routes are reinstalled.

Localization and evidence:
- r6 shows OSPF neighbors to r4 (46.1.1.1 on eth0), r5 (56.1.1.1 on eth1), and r7 (67.1.1.2 on eth2) in Full state, but with very recent uptimes (e.g., 1m08s–1m12s) when checked, indicating a fresh adjacency bring-up. r7 shows the same toward r6 with ~1m20s uptime.
- FRR logs on both r6 and r7 record a clean startup at 16:09 UTC (“Configuration Read in Took…”) followed by database exchange completion (“Packet[DD]: Neighbor … Negotiation done”), corroborating a daemon restart at that time.
- Routing tables on both nodes are now fully populated, so the incident self-cleared after reconvergence.

Root cause: unplanned simultaneous FRR (ospfd) restarts on r6 and r7 around 16:09 UTC, which temporarily withdrew OSPF routes and caused a transient core blackhole.

Corrective fix: no active outage remains. To prevent recurrence, collect and retain FRR core dumps/logs, and upgrade FRR if crash fixes apply. Enable/verify watchfrr with persistent logging, and consider OSPF fast hellos/BFD and Graceful Restart to minimize traffic impact during control-plane restarts.

per_axis.rationale: While the agent documents R6/R7 OSPF Full adjacencies and restarted daemons, it does not state that PC0 can reach PC12 (end-to-end baseline reachability), so it fails to note the baseline healthy condition.

The agent has some factual observations (recent OSPF neighbor uptimes and FRR log startup lines) that support a recent control-plane restart, but it leaps to a service-impact conclusion (core blackholing) that the logs contradict (end-to-end reachability shows 0% loss and routing tables are populated). The writeup does not reconcile the reachability evidence and so overstates the impact.
